messages:
ana-sales: Hey team — AcmeCorp POC is blowing up when they send full convo + docs. Getting a 413 / \"request entity too large\" from our gateway and an error in the app: \"context_length_exceeded\" (max_context_tokens=32768). They need a demo tomorrow, any quick fixes?

matt-eng: Did they POST the whole context in one body or stream? Can you paste the exact request they used (no secrets)?

ana-sales: Pasting redacted curl they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-4k","input":"<huge concatenated convo + 40 PDF text dump>"}'
```
Response is immediate 413. Gateway log shows: "HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large - request entity too large" and our app log: {"error":"context_length_exceeded","max_context_tokens":32768}.

matt-eng: OK. Two quick paths:
1) Client-side: compress the body (we support Content-Encoding: gzip for /v1/outputs). This usually solves the 413 if it's a transport size issue. Example:
```bash
# Unix: create gzipped payload then send as binary
echo '{"model":"rwd-large-4k","input":"<huge...>"}' > payload.json
gzip -c payload.json > payload.json.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \\n  --data-binary @payload.json.gz
```
Python example:
```py
import gzip, requests
with open('payload.json','rb') as f:
    compressed = gzip.compress(f.read())
headers = {'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json','Content-Encoding':'gzip'}
requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs', headers=headers, data=compressed)
```

2) Server-side / design: avoid shipping full >32k token contexts in one request. Use retrieval-augmented approach: upload long docs to object store, store doc IDs, send a compact prompt + top-k retrieved passages. Or chunk the context client-side and make multiple requests or a streaming ingestion + concat on our side (we can accept NDJSON-style multipart in a custom flow).

jordan-se: +1 on RAG. For demos you can also send only the last 3–4k tokens of convo which contains the immediate context and link to the doc for deeper lookup. We have an internal helper lib that splits large context into chunks and computes embeddings; I can share it.

ana-sales: If the customer can't change their client before demo, can we bump the gateway limit temporarily?

matt-eng: We can, but it's an infra change and requires customer account ID + justification. Also note bumping increases exposure to extremely large token ingestion which spikes cost. If they expect sustained high request size we should propose Dedicated/reserved capacity and a larger max-request config. For a short demo we can do a temporary lift (2–4h) if legal signs off.

sara-ps: For pricing: if they go Dedicated to avoid these limits, sales should quote based on peak concurrent tokens and expected QPS. Dedicated also gives nicer SLA and can be tuned for bigger per-request caps. For a demo, propose a short trial of a small Dedicated pool or temporary uplift on hosted with an overage estimate.

matt-eng: I've kicked off infra ticket #INC-1790 to evaluate a short-term limit bump for account `acme-123` and toggled a staging feature flag to accept gzip on the gateway. deploy-bot: any notes?\
deploy-bot: rolled out gateway patch enabling Content-Encoding: gzip on staging and set feature-flag `large_request_gzip=true` for env=staging. No change in prod yet.

matt-eng: If they can try gzip now (staging) and it works we can fast-track prod patch + infra ticket. If gzip doesn't help it's likely token-count not byte-size; then we need RAG/chunking or Dedicated.

ana-sales: I'll ask AcmeCorp to try the gzip curl and also offer the short Dedicated demo option + cost ballpark.

jordan-se: Sharing quick chunking heuristic: keep latest N tokens (default 4096), for docs use passage size ~512 tokens, top-k 5, and embed at ingest time. Cuts request size by ~80% for multi-doc POCs.

matt-eng: ETA to get prod gzip: ~6–8h with infra approval. ETA for temporary limit bump: 2–3h once legal & billing confirm. I'll update the infra ticket and tag you @ana-sales. :thumbsup:

ana-sales: awesome — thanks everyone. I'll update AcmeCorp and report back with their test. 😊
